title: test_leaks' pre-screens are tested against every kbcommon.SECRETS shape
goal: the planted-leak test of test_leaks.py, renamed to end in _and_leak_screens_cover_secrets (no new test id, no new test file), plants one string for each kbcommon.SECRETS pattern, assembled at run time, and asserts that there is one plant per pattern and that test_leaks.candidate() returns each plant's text and kbpublic.file_hits flags each as secret, so a future (?i) shape with an uppercase literal or class that the casefolded screen skips fails the suite

gates.question: How does the planted-leak test get its new name and its per-pattern plants?
options: Append the suffix to the existing name, plants in a secret_plants helper checked against their own pattern
Shorten the old name while renaming, plants inline in the test
gates.recommendation: Append the suffix to the existing name, plants in a secret_plants helper checked against their own pattern

notes: Found by the SP-wjp5qllo review (S3): ST-k3e4q43i (3c6ffe0d0) added screens() in test_leaks.py, compiling the (?i) screen without re.I and running it on t.casefold(); it is correct only because today's one (?i) shape has lowercase literals. A new shape with [A-Z] would make scan() skip a file the real check flags, and the test pass on a leak. SP-yyjwfjtc plan: still applies on origin/main b97cd6ebf (no test plants each SECRETS shape into candidate()). Premise run: planted one fake string per SECRETS pattern (13 patterns); today candidate(), kbpublic.file_hits and redact.redact catch every one, so the story adds the guard, not a fix. Base check: the selector collects no test (exit 2) until the rename.
